tradeoffs: Rust/Wasm implementation drives the DOM through wasm-bindgen glue; suite rows for this build: compressed size 48.8 vs React 51.4 (suite units, presumably kB), first paint 239.6 vs 226.6 ms, run memory 5.45 vs 4.37 MB, ready memory 1.77 vs 1.19 MB. Leptos 0.7 with csr, nightly and delegation features; benchmark-specific build.

README says Leptos is 'much faster at both creating and updating the UI than Yew'; in this data Leptos is 1.20x faster than Yew 0.23 on the same geometric mean (derived from page data).

compiler_and_flags: Swift to Wasm through @elementary-swift/vite-plugin-swift-wasm 0.2.0 and vite 8.3.1; Package.swift pins elementary-ui 0.8.0 and JavaScriptKit from 0.58.0 (Swift tools 6.3, SwiftWasm); whether Embedded Swift is used for the benchmark build and the swiftc flags are not stated in the files opened.
hardware: Not stated for the Chrome 154 snapshot (Chrome 154 results commit 2026-10-04); releases.json labels Chrome 144-146 'macOS' but gives no note for Chrome 148-154 and no CPU model.
tradeoffs: Swift compiled to Wasm; suite rows for this build: compressed size 143.7 vs React 51.4 (suite units, presumably kB), first paint 815.9 vs 226.6 ms, run memory 4.77 vs 4.37 MB. README advertises kB-sized Embedded Swift bundles but the suite shows a much larger compressed size and 3.6x slower first paint than React.
caveats: Independent suite, CPU model not stated, so tier B. Ratio is my own unweighted geometric mean from raw results.ts (derived from page data). The win over React is modest (1.14x) and comes from swap rows (React 89.7 ms vs 14.7 ms); on create 1,000 rows and create 10,000 rows ElementaryUI is slower than React (31.9 vs 23.6 ms, 349.6 vs 401.0 ms). Prebuilt bundle is checked in.
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch restricted to news.ycombinator.com ('Show HN AssemblyScript faster than JavaScript WebAssembly benchmark', 'WebAssembly: TinyGo vs. Rust vs. AssemblyScript', 'Is WebAssembly faster than JavaScript?' threads) only returned discussion with no linked repo, so the candidate came from github.com/topics/webassembly and the krausest/js-framework-benchmark raw results.ts file.

name: LUME Kiwi (kiwi.js)
workload: Benchmark.js ops/sec for constraint-solver object creation and for solving, kiwi versus Cassowary.js (bench/ in the repo, run with npm run bench).
claimed_speedup: README sample output: creation 26,243 ops/sec vs Cassowary.js 2,597 ops/sec ('Fastest is kiwi (± 10.11x faster)'); solving 595,455 ops/sec vs 260,002 ops/sec ('± 2.29x faster').
tradeoffs: Pure TypeScript/JavaScript library; README says it will 'soon' be compiled to WebAssembly with AssemblyScript, but no Wasm build is shipped. Originally created by Chris Colbert (nucleic kiwi), redesigned by Lume.
caveats: Sample output only, with no CPU model, Node or browser version, or flags. This is JavaScript beating JavaScript, so it is off-category for the Wasm-languages slice; the claim is also not Wasm-based. Result is the README sample, not a recorded run. Cassowary.js is an older, unmaintained baseline.
